claims.wording: Cindori markets Sensei as a Mac system monitoring utility.
claims.excerpt: The All-in-One Mac System Performance Monitoring Tool.
claims.scope: Vendor positioning, not measured superiority.

claims.wording: The product page documents Intel and Apple Silicon Mac support.
claims.excerpt: Get in-depth insights into system performance and hardware health for Intel and Apple Silicon Macs.
claims.scope: No native compatibility testing performed.

claims.wording: Sensei offers customizable status-bar/dropdown monitoring panels.
claims.excerpt: Customize widgets for the status bar or dropdown panel, and create personalized monitoring dashboards with your own design and tracking preferences.
claims.scope: Documented feature; no performance test.

claims.wording: Sensei documents removal of caches, logs, large downloads and leftover installation files.
claims.excerpt: including old caches, system logs, large downloads, and leftover installation files.
claims.scope: Does not establish safety, completeness, exact current deletion semantics or measured savings.

claims.wording: Sensei documents app uninstallation with related leftover files.
claims.excerpt: Remove Apps and Their Leftover Files.
claims.scope: Vendor feature claim, not proof every leftover is removed.

claims.wording: Sensei documents drive S.M.A.R.T. analysis.
claims.excerpt: The Drive Health Report in Sensei will provide you with a S.M.A.R.T analysis of your storage.
claims.scope: No guarantee of failure prediction or support for every drive/enclosure.

claims.wording: Sensei documents battery-health, thermal and disk-benchmark tools.
claims.excerpt: Sensei’s Disk Benchmark tool measures the read and write speeds of your Mac’s storage with a single click.
claims.scope: Other supporting sections: MacBook Battery Health Monitoring; Real-Time Mac Thermal Monitoring. No benchmark executed.

claims.wording: Sensei documents battery cycle count, capacity and real-time performance insights.
claims.excerpt: including cycle count, capacity, and real-time performance.
claims.scope: Vendor documentation; not an observed battery-health measurement.

claims.wording: Sensei documents CPU/GPU temperatures, fan speeds and system heat views.
claims.excerpt: Monitor CPU and GPU temperatures, fan speeds, and system heat levels to diagnose hardware issues.
claims.scope: Documented monitoring, not proof of a diagnosis or fan control on all hardware.

claims.wording: The store displays $29 billed annually for up to three Macs.
claims.excerpt:
Valid for up to 3 Macs.
$29
Billed annually.
claims.scope: Dollar symbol as displayed; ISO currency, taxes and checkout localization unverified. Not a free app.

claims.wording: The store displays $59 as a one-time purchase for up to three Macs.
claims.excerpt:
Valid for up to 3 Macs.
$59
One Time Purchase.
claims.scope: Do not call it lifetime updates or normalize to USD without evidence.

claims.wording: The regular licence includes updates to versions 1 and 2; version 3 onward may be paid upgrades.
claims.excerpt: The Regular License grants you access to all upcoming updates to the current major version of Sensei (1), as well as version 2. Version 3 and onwards may be a paid upgrade.
claims.scope: Store still calls 1 current; newer vendor article discusses 2.1.2. Preserve explicit update entitlement, not the stale current-version label.

claims.wording: The subscription licence key expires if the subscription expires without renewal.
claims.excerpt: If your subscription expires and is not renewed, your license key will expire.
claims.scope: No paid subscription tested.

claims.wording: The advertised refund window ends at activation even if fewer than fourteen days have elapsed.
claims.excerpt: Refunds are available within 14 days of purchase before license activation.
claims.scope: Do not advertise an unconditional fourteen-day money-back guarantee.

claims.wording: Licences are per user, up to three machines where that person is the primary user; businesses need enough licences for their users.
claims.excerpt: Licenses are per user and valid for use on all supported operating systems.
claims.scope: Supporting same paragraph limits to 3 unique machines and says businesses need at least as many licences as users. Not three unrestricted business seats.

claims.wording: Cindori owns the software copyright and supplies a commercial EULA.
claims.excerpt: All title, including but not limited to copyrights, in and to SOFTWARE PRODUCT and any copies thereof are owned by CINDORI AB.
claims.scope: Treat as proprietary commercial licensing; no official open-source repository established.

claims.wording: A vendor article dated August 14, 2026 identifies Sensei 2.1.2 and macOS 14+.
claims.excerpt: Current Sensei 2.1.2 requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later
claims.scope: Version-specific vendor documentation, not proof of the latest downloadable build in October. Hardware/runtime not tested.

claims.wording: Cindori provides Sensei 1.5.10 for older Macs and warns it may have more bugs.
claims.excerpt: Download Sensei 1.5.10
claims.scope: The same page says Catalina was supported at launch but minimum OS has since risen. Never apply 10.15 to current Sensei.

claims.wording: Sensei 1.6 introduced an approved LaunchDaemon and integrated the menu-bar monitor into the main app.
claims.excerpt: Sensei 1.6 replaces the helper tool with a modern LaunchDaemon.
claims.scope: May 17, 2025 release-specific architecture. Do not infer exact 2.x onboarding from this history.

claims.wording: Disk Sensei and Sensei are related but separately introduced products in Cindori’s history.
claims.excerpt: We released Disk Sensei, a comprehensive disk utility to monitor drive health, analyze storage usage, and optimize performance
claims.scope: About timeline: Disk Sensei 2015; Sensei 2019. Do not claim a simple rename or identical binaries.

claims.wording: Cindori offers an upgrade from Disk Sensei or Trim Enabler to Sensei.
claims.excerpt: Purchased Trim Enabler or Disk Sensei in the past? Upgrade to Sensei at up to 50% off.
claims.scope: Separate predecessor/upgrade relationship, not proof Trim Enabler is the same product. Eligibility requires prior purchase verification; no form submitted.

claims.wording: The vendor article says some Sensei cleaning features require Full Disk Access.
claims.excerpt: Some Sensei cleaning features require Full Disk Access.
claims.scope: Attributed documentation; no permission changes made.

claims.wording: Breathing Room is a free maintenance preview; AI Care is optional at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year.
claims.excerpt: **AI Care is optional: $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year.**
claims.scope: Current README agrees with 2026-10-21 live verification register. No checkout test.

claims.wording: Breathing Room requires macOS 13+, Python 3.10+ for disk inventory, and internet/sign-in for hosted agent features.
claims.excerpt: **Python 3.10+** for disk inventory and legacy cleanup scripts.
claims.scope: Universal Intel/Apple Silicon installer; physical Intel runtime remains untested. Local storage/process tools do not require AI Care.

claims.wording: The Breathing Room preview is not notarized.
claims.excerpt: The preview is not notarized.
claims.scope: Release notes also disclose Apple Development, not Developer ID signing; never recommend disabling protections.

claims.wording: Breathing Room documents category/app/project/folder/large-file views and grouped helper CPU/memory inspection.
claims.excerpt: Use **Apps** to inspect CPU and memory use across an app and its helpers.
claims.scope: Partial permissions and cached inventory possible; sampled ownership is not forensic writer attribution.

claims.wording: Daily care reuses exact approved locations and methods while Breathing Room remains running.

Scheduled care cleans only exact locations and methods you
previously approved; newly discovered locations wait for review.
claims.scope: No wake-from-sleep/post-quit guarantee. Source architecture, not distributed-runtime certification.

workflow.title: Mac storage pressure or drive trouble? Choose the right investigation
workflow.primaryIntent: Separate lack of capacity from drive-health questions before choosing a cleanup action.
workflow.description: Capacity and drive-health indicators answer different questions. Use Sensei’s documented hardware views or Breathing Room’s storage workflow without treating either as a diagnosis or a cleanup guarantee.
outline: Start with the reader’s symptom: full storage versus a drive-health warning; neither proves the other.
Check capacity and identify known files before considering removal; a large file is not permission.
Explain Sensei’s documented S.M.A.R.T., thermal and benchmark tools without promising prediction or a repair.
Use Breathing Room, which we build, for storage categories/app/project investigation and reviewable cleanup; disclose preview/Python/hosted constraints.
Preserve backup and app-native management options; no destructive tests or TRIM/security-setting tutorial.
Finish with a decision checklist: capacity, hardware concern, or both.
visuals: sensei-drive-health immediately after lead with historical caption
current-space-browser-preview alongside capacity discussion; preserve example banner
workflow.interactionPass: Propose a static three-path decision aid (capacity / health warning / both), not a simulated scanner or unsupported numeric score.
workflow.exclusion: Not another generic cleaner list or CPU troubleshooting post; no fabricated diagnosis, hands-on trial, savings or performance claims.
workflow.wordCount: Earned length, approximately 900–1400 words; no padding.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs Sensei: storage workflows or hardware diagnostics
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose between overlapping Mac maintenance products by documented workflow and deployment caveats.
structure: Who should consider the Breathing Room preview

sensei: Documented S.M.A.R.T., thermal, battery and benchmark tools; choose for hardware-oriented investigation, not guaranteed diagnosis.
Configurable menu-bar panels and app uninstallation documented; subscription or one-time licence for up to three Macs subject to per-user/update terms.
Latest build verification, cleanup semantics, detailed developer adapters and network behavior remain unknown.
breathingRoom: Source/register documents category/app/project storage views, grouped helper inspection and exact saved approvals; potential fit for recurring investigation, not proof of superiority.
Free local core with optional paid hosted AI Care; preview not notarized, Python prerequisite and physical Intel untested. Hosted AI is not offline.
No verified equivalence to Sensei’s hardware diagnostics or app uninstaller; do not imply either parity or an unsupported absence.
